messages:
kevin: quick flag 1: bringup of rerank-v5 (ptq int8) shows ndcg@10 flat but MRR head (top1) drop ~8% on paraphrase-heavy slice. weird because overall scores look fine. anyone seen dedupe normalizer interact badly with quant?
leila: did the dedupe step change? we pushed a new normalizer that canonicalizes punctuation + whitespace last week.
omar: i reviewed the normalizer: it collapses repeated punctuation and lowercases; also does a short paraphrase hash to dedupe near-duplicates. that hash function was updated to use murmur3->xxhash.
kevin: parity check: offline eval harness used old murmur3 hashes (baseline), prod bringup used xxhash (candidate). could hashing change candidate pool ordering?
leila: yes, if dedupe filter removes different candidate(s) the top1 can flip. but it shouldn't cause systematic MRR head loss unless the removed candidates were often correct answers.
omar: hypothesis: xxhash has different collision profile causing more aggressive dedupe for very short candidates (titles/snippets). those are often the exact gold for short queries.
kevin: can we run a controlled replay: apply old dedupe vs new dedupe to the same raw candidate set and compare top1 overlaps?
omar: doing that now. quick script: ```python
old_hash = lambda s: murmur3(s)
new_hash = lambda s: xxhash(s)
old_keep = dedupe(candidates, key=old_hash)
new_keep = dedupe(candidates, key=new_hash)
metrics = compare_top1(old_keep, new_keep)
print(metrics)
```
leila: also consider interaction with PTQ score compression. maybe new dedupe keeps slightly longer candidate that when quantized gets score-squeezed and falls behind, shifting top1. we should test candidate set parity *before* model scoring.
eval-bot: quick replay summary (N=5k paraphrase-heavy queries):
- candidate parity: 98.6% identical after dedupe (old vs new)
- top1 divergence on identical sets: 3.2%
- MRR delta when swapping dedupe only (float baseline): -0.4%
- MRR delta when swapping dedupe + ptq int8: -7.9%
kevin: that suggests a two-way interaction: dedupe change mild alone, but amplifies with quantization.
omar: two mitigation paths: 1) revert hashing to murmur3 for canary until we re-eval, 2) apply a post-quant "score temperature" to slightly spread logits before argmax to reduce head ties.
leila: temperature hack might mask the root cause; prefer to freeze dedupe and re-run PTQ calibration on candidate sets produced by xxhash to be thorough.
kevin: agree. short plan: A) revert dedupe hashing on current canary, B) run PTQ calibration with xxhash-produced candidate corpus (calib job id calib-1766-x), C) run a tiny microbench to measure top1_tie_fraction and head_shift.
omar: i'll open a revert PR for dedupe hashing and add a regression test that ensures dedupe parity on a golden candidate snapshot.
eval-bot: scheduled jobs: calib-1766-x (queued), microbench-1766-y (pending).
leila: also add a guard in onboarding: "if dedupe/hash algo changes, regenerate calibration corpus and run top1 parity check vs baseline golds". small checklist item.
kevin: i'll update the runbook and roll the revert. thanks folks. we'll monitor canary and re-run metrics after calib job finishes. :eyes:
